- Western intelligence agencies, including Germany's **BND** and armed forces, believe **Russia** is ready to launch a nuclear-armed satellite called **Sputnik-S**, Reuters reported, citing NDR, WDR and Sueddeutsche Zeitung[3].
- The satellite was reportedly built years ago and stored near Moscow. Warnings shared among NATO members in early November said it could launch within 60 days[3][8].
- The Russian embassy in Berlin rejected the claims as propaganda. Such a deployment would violate the 1967 **Outer Space Treaty**, which bans weapons of mass destruction in orbit[2].
